https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/25/the-.text: The United States Army is reportedly taking preparatory steps for a possible operation involving Cuba, according to an exclusive published on Friday by CBS News, which obtained an internal Army message and spoke with several US officials familiar with the plans.The US Army Reserve is examining whether it can provide US Southern Command with Military Police forces, medical staff and other support units within a period of 90 to 120 days, according to the document reviewed by CBS News.The internal message does not explicitly mention Cuba. However, several US officials told the outlet, on condition of anonymity, that the request forms part of the military planning the United States is carrying out in relation to the island.For the moment, there is no indication that any unit has been ordered to deploy, and the document does not specify where the forces would be sent or what kind of operation they would take part in.Medical, logistics and military police unitsAccording to the US network, the document requests information on the availability of six types of units that could be placed under the authority of US Southern Command, which is responsible for US military operations in Central America, South America and the Caribbean.These include units specialising in logistics, transport, maintenance, fuel and supplies, as well as an engineer battalion.The request also covers a medical brigade, teams capable of providing emergency surgery and treatment for wounded troops close to deployed forces, and a Military Police brigade, typically used for security, detention and other policing tasks.A Southern Command spokesman contacted by CBS News declined to give details of possible movements or deployment timelines for operational security reasons, and said the command continually assesses military needs within its area of responsibility.'A small neighbouring country' posing no threatThe report comes after months of rising tensions and threats from US President Donald Trump, who this week told the UN General Assembly that Cuba "is a failed state" and that it "will fall".Meanwhile, Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez stated in an interview with NBC News on Friday that the United States "will never be able to find justification" for launching a military attack against Cuba, and he dismissed the idea that the island would suffer the same fate as Venezuela:"The U.S. government will never be able to find justification or any reason whatsoever to launch a military attack against a small neighbouring country that in no way poses a threat to its national security," he asserted.

Official news Home page Official news 0 0 President Ilham Aliyev: 96% of Azerbaijan’s territory is supplied with gas © APA | Ilham Aliyev, President of the Republic of Azerbaijan 26 September 2026 09:34 (UTC +04:00) Ninety-six percent of Azerbaijan’s territory is supplied with gas, President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev said during his speech at an event on the theme “Rebuilding Trust in a Fragmented World: The South Caucasus as a Pillar of Global Connectivity and Investment Stability,” held as part of the 2nd Azerbaijan International Investment Forum in Baku, APA reports. The President said the country has one of the highest gasification rates. “Ninety-six percent of Azerbaijan’s territory is supplied with gas. One hundred percent of the country’s population is provided with electricity and broadband internet. At the same time, we export electricity,” the head of state emphasized. Ilham Aliyev noted that, in terms of domestic needs, almost all the work has been completed and there may not be much need for additional projects. “Work on railway infrastructure has also been almost completed. We have nine international airports and seaports. Thus, when it comes to domestic infrastructure, we are in a good position,” the President said. The head of state noted that infrastructure serving multinational interests could be more attractive. According to him, this primarily includes transportation, logistics and physical infrastructure, as well as administrative and digital infrastructure. “We can build many bridges, overpasses and ships. However, if we do not properly take into account modern trends in digitalization and customs procedures, and if we do not facilitate and accelerate cargo handling, we will lose in the competition,” Ilham Aliyev emphasized. The President said electricity transmission lines are another important area, noting that there is great potential in this field. “Today, Azerbaijan is not the only source of energy. Less than two years ago, we signed an agreement with Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan on laying an underwater electricity cable across the Caspian Sea. The goal is to connect Central Asia with Azerbaijan and then with Europe through electricity,” the head of state said. Ilham Aliyev said the implementation of this project will require significant financial resources. The President noted that another important project is the Black Sea underwater electricity cable, which is already at the feasibility study stage. “This cable will also run from Azerbaijan to Georgia and then to Romania. We are talking about a 4-gigawatt project aimed at the European energy market,” the head of state emphasized. Ilham Aliyev also noted the need for energy storage systems. “All this is necessary not only for us, but also for broader international cooperation. I think these will be the main areas of interest,” the President added. https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: William Chapman died after he climbed into the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park. Photograph: South Yorkshire police/PA View image in fullscreen William Chapman died after he climbed into the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park. Photograph: South Yorkshire police/PA South Yorkshire NHS staff investigated over potential accessing of tiger victim’s records Yorkshire ambulance service says workers may have accessed or attempted to access information ‘without legitimate reason’ Robyn Vinter North of England correspondent Fri 16 Oct 2026 12.45 EDT Last modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 13.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google NHS staff may have accessed the medical records of a man killed by a tiger at a wildlife park “without legitimate permission”, an ambulance trust has said. Yorkshire ambulance service NHS trust has launched an investigation into two members of staff at the trust, which responded to emergency calls on Saturday when William Chapman climbed into the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park. There may have been “two instances involving two members of staff accessing or attempting to access incident/medical information without a legitimate reason”, the ambulance service said after being contacted by HSJ, the trade publication for NHS policy. Chapman, 23, was mauled to death by the 200kg male Siberian tiger named Altai at the zoo after climbing into its enclosure. The park reopened on Friday after being closed since the attack. An inquest opening on Thursday heard how Chapman had schizophrenia and had experienced bouts of psychosis but was “highly functioning and independent with no care requirements”. Family of man killed by tiger criticise online content after Trump reposts video Read more His family, who did not attend the hearing at Doncaster coroner’s court, expressed concerns about his contact with mental health services before his death. Rotherham, Doncaster and South Humber NHS foundation trust has launched an investigation into its contact with him. The inquest heard Chapman was a self-employed online trader who was living in Doncaster at the time of his death. An initial postmortem found that he died from multiple traumatic injuries. The coroner’s officer Caitlin Brookes said: “He was approached by the tiger and the ensuing physical contact between the tiger and Mr Chapman led to him sustaining multiple traumatic injuries which rapidly led to his death.” Park staff secured the tiger and Yorkshire ambulance service paramedics attended and confirmed Chapman’s death at the scene. The senior coroner Nicola Mundy said her office was awaiting a more substantial report on the extent of Chapman’s injuries ahead of a full inquest on 18 March. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion The potential breach of Chapman’s medical records happened after the attack and has been reported to the Information Commissioner’s Office. The trust said it had “identified an information governance concern in relation to this tragic incident at Yorkshire Wildlife Park and William’s family has been informed of our ongoing investigation into this. We believe there may have been two instances involving two members of staff accessing or attempting to access incident/medical information following this incident without a legitimate reason to do so.” It said: “We take the confidentiality and security of patient information extremely seriously and have robust systems in place to protect information, and this concern has been identified as a result of our proactive audits.” Ahead of reopening on Friday, Yorkshire Wildlife Park said safety was the “highest priority”, and it thanked members of the public who had sent “messages of support and love for our team at this time”. Wildlife and zoo experts have told the Guardian it is unlikely the wildlife park could have done anything to prevent the death.
